provenance.title: Antenatal care contact schedule
provenance.primarySource: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience (2016); WHO SMART ANC ANCS01
provenance.why: The 2016 model replaced four focused visits with eight contacts, because the evidence showed more contact reduces perinatal death. The word is 'contact', not 'visit', on purpose: it includes community and outreach contact, and the schedule must not silently assume a facility.

sourceVerification.vendoredArtefact: docs/reference/who-dak/smart-anc — ANCS01.cql supplies the 8-contact timing and EDD = LMP + 280 days
sourceVerification.note: The contact WEEKS are taken from the vendored ANCS01 logic. The window widths around each contact (how early a contact may count, how late before it is overdue) are an engineering seed — the guideline names target gestations, not tolerances — and each is stated so a ministry can set it. blocksRatification stays true until the windows are ratified.

contacts.name: First contact
contacts.note: By 12 weeks. This is the contact that dates the pregnancy, and dating is only reliable early — a first contact in the third trimester cannot be redated by a scan.

contacts.name: Sixth contact
keyActions: Assess presentation — refer breech for review

contacts.name: Seventh contact
keyActions: Confirm place of birth and transport

contacts.name: Eighth contact
contacts.note: At 40 weeks. Beyond this the pregnancy is post-term and the question changes from routine care to a plan for birth, so the schedule does not simply keep counting contacts — it hands over to post-term surveillance.
keyActions: Plan for post-term surveillance if not yet delivered

postTerm.message: The pregnancy is post-term. Routine contacts no longer apply; this needs an active plan for birth and increased fetal surveillance.
postTerm.note: A separate state, not a ninth contact. Counting contacts past term would report a woman at 42 weeks as merely due for another routine check.

adaptation.whoStatement: A minimum of eight antenatal contacts is recommended, at weeks 12, 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38 and 40.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published. The contact windows around each target are an engineering seed pending ratification.
evidenceRefs: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience (2016)
